slides.headline: Istanbul hunted a ‘lioness’. It wasn’t a lion
slides.subline: **70+ officers, drones and thermal cameras** searched woodland near Istanbul.
slides.credit: Mostafameraji / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Belgrade Forest, file photo)

slides.body: Police spotted a big cat on **security cameras** in Zekeriyaköy, in Istanbul’s Sarıyer district. Officials said it was a [[lioness]] and closed nearby woodland.
More than [[70 personnel]] joined in, backed by **drones, vets and thermal imaging**. The governor’s office said the aim was to capture it **alive**.
The district mayor said the animal had not harmed **chickens** it passed. His theory: it was hand-reared. He still warned people to treat it as [[dangerous]].
Then came new footage. Turkish authorities now say it was [[not a lion]]. The animal was seen in a private garden. Officials have not said what species it was.
One blurry camera frame sent a whole city into **panic**. Would you have believed it was a lion too? Tell us below.
